newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end higher on optimism, lower bond yield.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end higher on optimism, lower bond yield.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Monday as a decline in the U.S. long bond yield gave prices a lift and market optimism kept selling interest at a minimum, traders said.
The Hang Seng index ended up 123.63 points at 13,517.56, its session high. Turnover was HK$7.38 billion.
"People who are long and overweight in the market, they don't see any major bad news on the horizon to sell stocks," said analyst Paul Chan of Merrill Lynch Asset Management.
"Valuations are a little bit stretched but valuation alone cannot trigger any sell-off," he said.
Others said market participants were also reacting to movement in the bond market and that while there were still buyers around, very few were keen to sell.
"I think people are reacting to the movement of the bond market. There is some buying around and more importantly there is no selling," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
On Friday, the U.S. long bond rose 31/32, bringing the yield down to 6.36 percent, its lowest level since March 4.
Analysts expected market undertones to remain buoyant for the rest of the week.
"There is still some momentum to go up. Interest rates will remain low without any inflationary pressure," said an analyst with a local firm.
Chinese companies and those steeped in business on the mainland tended to be better received with the return of Hong Kong to China in mid-1997 increasingly seen as an asset, some said.
"What liability? People buy Chinese stocks, buy Hong Kong companies with China exposure," Chan said.
"People are willing to pay a premium for those sorts of companies."
Property stocks continued to edge higher, with Henderson Land ending HK$1.75 higher at HK$79.50 and Cheung Kong rising HK$1.50 to HK$69.50.
HSBC Holdings ended at HK$162.50, up HK$1.50.
